papers.title: Trends in Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Disease Management, and Predicted Cardiovascular Risk Among US Adults, 1999-2023
papers.summary: You described 4 effects with terms related to 'marginally significant'.

findings.sentence: Diabetes prevalence increased significantly in most subgroups, although trends differed significantly only by race and Hispanic origin (P for interaction = 0.016).
Dyslipidemia trends differed significantly by age (P for interaction <0.001) and education (P = 0.011).
Trends differed significantly by income (P for interaction = 0.005), with a significant decline observed only in the highest-income group (OR, 0.85).

Myocardial infarction also showed a significant declining trend (OR, 0.89; P = 0.017), although the difference between the first and last cycles was borderline significant (3.6% to 2.8%; P for change = 0.051).
